'You're making MORE work during a crisis!' She's furious. You're dragged back to your crib, and the botched self-change becomes a cautionary tale. She diapers you roughly while lecturing about 'patients who make everything harder.' Other patients saw your failed attempt. Your inability to successfully change yourself has proven you need supervision for even basic tasks.
failure.statusEffect: Failed Self-Care: Made disaster trying to change yourself. -35% on independence checks. Staff doesn't trust you with basic tasks. Mockery from other patients. Lasts 5 encounters.

choices.label: Have a genuine tantrum to get immediate attention

success.narration: You've been patient long enough. You need attention NOW. You let yourself slip into genuine regression - not performance, but real emotional dysregulation. You start crying - real tears, loud sobs. Then escalate - banging your hands on the crib rails, kicking your legs, screaming. 'NEED CHANGE! NEED HELP! NOW NOW NOW!' The tantrum is complete, genuine, regressed. Nurse Sarah rushes over immediately - tantrums during crises are priority because they can trigger other patients. 'Okay baby, okay. Shhhh.' She doesn't punish you - she treats it as a genuine regression episode. She picks you up despite being busy, holds you while you sob, rocks you gently. 'I know, I know. Too long waiting. Poor baby.' She changes you immediately, talking soothingly the whole time. When you've calmed, she gives you a pacifier and extra cuddles. Your tantrum is treated as emotional breakdown rather than manipulation. Later notes read: 'Patient regressed under stress of delayed care. Genuine littlespace achieved. Requires more frequent attention to maintain stability.' Your real regression has actually gotten you reclassified as needing more care attention.
success.statusEffect: Deep Regression: Genuine breakdown during crisis. +35% on REGRESSION checks. Staff treats you as more deeply regressed. Priority attention during future shortages. More coddling overall.

failure.narration: You decide a tantrum will get attention fast. You start screaming and crying - but it's clearly fake. Your voice is too controlled, your movements too calculated. Nurse Sarah glances over and immediately recognizes it as manipulation. 'Oh no you don't.' Instead of rushing to help, she ignores you completely. Your tantrum escalates but so do other patients' - real ones, genuine distress. Staff prioritize those. You're left screaming in your crib, being ignored, for over an hour. When finally addressed, Sarah is not gentle. 'That performance was pathetic. You threw a fake tantrum during a crisis to manipulate priority?' She checks your diaper roughly - yes, you need changing, but now she's not sympathetic. The change is quick, rough, without any tenderness. 'Patients who fake regression to manipulate get remembered.' Your obviously fake tantrum has marked you as a manipulator, lost you any sympathy, and still didn't get you faster service. Other patients who had real breakdowns got comfort; you got contempt.
failure.statusEffect: Fake Tantrum: Obvious manipulation attempt. -40% on REGRESSION checks. Staff doesn't believe your emotional displays. Other patients saw the fakery. Trust severely damaged. Lasts 7 encounters.

events.scene: The ward suddenly becomes uncomfortably warm. The heating system has malfunctioned, pushing the temperature to an uncomfortable 85 degrees. Patients are sweating in their thick diapers and onesies. Staff scramble to fix the issue while trying to keep patients comfortable. Nurse Diana approaches with bottles of cool water. 'We need to keep everyone hydrated while maintenance fixes the heat. Drink up.' The problem is that drinking lots of fluids while in thick, already-warm diapers is a recipe for frequent changes - except staff are busy with the temperature crisis. Some patients are already showing signs of diaper rash from the heat and humidity. Others are whining about discomfort. The oppressive warmth makes everything worse - diapers feel heavier, clothing clings, and patience runs thin.

choices.label: Drink the water and endure the discomfort without complaint

success.narration: You drink the cool water gratefully despite knowing it'll mean needing to pee soon. The heat is intense, sweat beading on your forehead. Your thick diaper feels like a furnace between your legs but you don't complain. You focus on breathing, staying calm, accepting the discomfort. After an hour, the cooling system is repaired and the temperature drops. Nurse Diana checks on you. 'How are you holding up?' You're sweaty, your diaper is soaked from both sweat and wetting yourself, but you've stayed calm. 'I managed,' you say simply. She checks you for rash and is surprised to find minimal irritation despite the conditions. 'Your skin held up well. And you didn't complain once even though I know you were uncomfortable.' She changes you into a lighter diaper, applies cooling powder, and gives you a popsicle as a reward for endurance. 'You have good tolerance for physical discomfort. That's noted.' Your stoic endurance of genuinely bad conditions has proven your resilience.
success.statusEffect: Heat Endurance: Handled crisis conditions well. +20% on GRIT checks. Staff knows you can tolerate discomfort without breaking down.

failure.narration: You drink the water but the heat becomes unbearable. Your diaper is soaked with sweat and urine, the padding clinging uncomfortably to your skin. You try to stay calm but can't. 'It's too hot! This diaper is too much!' You start pulling at your clothing, trying to remove your onesie. Staff rush over. 'Stop that! You need to stay dressed.' But you're genuinely overheating, becoming dizzy. Your body isn't handling the heat well. They have to move you to a cooler isolation area and remove your outer clothing, leaving you in just a diaper. A fan is pointed at you. You lie there, miserable, while other patients managed to endure in the main ward. When temperature is restored, you're brought back. Other patients and staff saw you couldn't handle what everyone else endured. 'Some patients have lower heat tolerance,' a nurse notes clinically. Your inability to endure the temporary discomfort has marked you as having lower physical resilience than peers.
failure.statusEffect: Heat Sensitive: Couldn't handle temporary temperature crisis. -25% on GRIT checks. Seen as having low physical tolerance. May be excluded from some activities. Lasts 4 encounters.

choices.label: Suggest removing unnecessary clothing layers to cool down

success.narration: 'Nurse Diana, if the heat is this bad and will take time to fix, could we remove some clothing layers? Onesies and pants over diapers are making it worse. Just diapers and t-shirts would help us regulate temperature better.' Your suggestion is practical, smart. She pauses, considers, then nods. 'That's... actually sensible medical advice. Let me check with the supervisor.' Within minutes, approval comes through. Staff begin removing outer layers from willing patients - onesies come off, pants removed, leaving patients in just t-shirts and diapers. The difference is immediate. You feel significantly cooler. Other patients look relieved. The supervisor approaches you personally. 'That was good thinking. Quick adaptation to changing conditions.' Your practical suggestion has improved conditions for everyone. Later, she makes notes: 'Patient provided constructive solution during facility crisis. Demonstrated problem-solving and medical reasoning.' Your intelligent adaptation has proven you can think practically even in uncomfortable situations.
success.statusEffect: Problem Solver: Suggested solution that helped everyone. +25% on WIT checks. Staff values your practical thinking. Consulted during future issues.

failure.narration: 'This is ridiculous! Just turn the heat down! How hard is that?!' Your 'suggestion' comes out as complaint rather than constructive problem-solving. Nurse Diana's expression hardens. 'Do you think we're CHOOSING to keep it hot? Maintenance is working on it. Complaining doesn't fix mechanical failures.' Your entitled tone has annoyed already-stressed staff. 'If you can't handle temporary discomfort, maybe you need different accommodations.' They move you to an isolation room - it's slightly cooler but you're alone, removed from the group. You miss the eventual solution (removing clothing layers) that other patients got. When brought back after the heat is fixed, other patients are comfortable in just diapers and t-shirts, having had relief. You were stuck in full clothing in isolation. Your complaint rather than constructive suggestion resulted in worse treatment and missing the group solution.
failure.statusEffect: Complainer: Whined instead of problem-solving. -25% on WIT checks. Staff annoyed with you. Other patients got better treatment. Lasts 4 encounters.

choices.label: Refuse the water to avoid wetting your diaper in the heat

success.narration: 'I don't want the water. I'm okay.' Nurse Diana frowns. 'You need to stay hydrated in this heat.' You shake your head. 'I'd rather not. The diaper is already uncomfortable enough without adding more liquid.' She studies you. 'You're... choosing to be uncomfortable to avoid wetting? That's unusual.' She respects your choice though. Over the next two hours, you're the only patient who doesn't drink. You're also the only one whose diaper doesn't become thoroughly soaked. When the heat is finally fixed, you're thirsty and uncomfortable but your diaper is only damp from sweat, not sodden with urine like everyone else's. Nurse Diana checks you. 'Your diaper is in much better condition than others'. That was smart - avoiding unnecessary liquid intake during a crisis where changes would be delayed.' She offers you water now, and you drink gratefully. 'You exercised good judgment about bladder management during difficult conditions.' Your choice to prioritize staying dry over immediate comfort has been recognized as strategic thinking.
success.statusEffect: Strategic Bladder Control: Managed liquid intake wisely during crisis. +30% on BLADDER checks. Staff notes your planning ability. Earned emergency bathroom privileges.

failure.narration: 'I'm not drinking that. I don't want to wet my diaper in this heat.' Nurse Diana's expression turns stern. 'Hydration during heat isn't optional. You'll drink or we'll administer fluids another way.' You refuse stubbornly. Two orderlies appear. They hold you while Diana forces a bottle into your mouth, tipping it so you either swallow or choke. The water floods in, making you gulp desperately. They make you finish two full bottles while restrained. 'Patients don't refuse medical necessities.' Now you're left in your crib, force-hydrated, with the inevitable result. Your bladder fills rapidly in the heat. Within thirty minutes you desperately need to pee. Within an hour, your control breaks and you flood your diaper. But here's the cruel part - because you refused to drink voluntarily, they leave you in the wet diaper longer as punishment. 'Patients who refuse hydration get last priority for changes.' You sit in your hot, soaked diaper for two miserable hours before finally being changed. Your refusal resulted in the exact outcome you tried to avoid, but worse - forced fluid intake and then being left in wetness as punishment.
failure.statusEffect: Forced Hydration: Refused medical care and was forced. -35% on BLADDER checks. Staff doesn't trust your judgment. Left longer in wet diapers as consequence. Lasts 6 encounters.
